evidence.quote: This morning I will give a retrospective on the first five years of supervisory stress testing, highlighting some of the accomplishments and identifying some areas in which we may consider changes in the future.
The firms participating in CCAR have more than doubled their tier 1 common capital since 2009, an increase of $500 billion of additional, high-quality capital in the U.S. financial system.
In devising recession scenarios, we draw on many of the same macroeconomic modeling tools used in making monetary policy.

parsed.rationale: The speech addresses supervisory stress testing and CCAR capital planning, not monetary policy, inflation, or the economic outlook. It carries no monetary policy signal, so the stance is neutral.
